clue.text: Making an enemy of a right awful giant

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the letters of giant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turns against a dreadful giant, perhaps in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like the direction R, but here it is the legal claim on property; 'awful' signals the anagram of the giant.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them hostile, making them an enemy.

clue.text: See old male come into view

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Watch an elderly man appear.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear, often indistinctly and threateningly, as a shape coming into view.

clue.text: Former nurse making offer

parts.note: ex means former
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A one-time nurse is making a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to extend an invitation or help is to offer it.

clue.text: Ring girl? You will, you confess finally

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A suitor asks a girl to admit she will accept the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes U, L, U and S from 'You will, you confess'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulus is a ring-shaped figure, the region between two concentric circles.

clue.text: Bird — is one black on top?

indicators.note: on top says, in this down clue, the first letters sit above the word is

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird has a black head.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill.

clue.text: Information on container that protects a plant

indicators.note: on in this down clue says the information word sits above the rest

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: that protects says the container wraps around the letter a

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A label on a pot that shields a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that protects' puts A inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentian is a mountain plant known for its deep blue flowers.

clue.text: Winchester's recycling facility?

parts.note: a winchester is a large glass bottle, so its recycling point would be a bank for bottles

explanation.surface: Where the city of Winchester sends its waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winchester' suggests the English city or the rifle, but it is also a large bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for collecting empty glass for recycling, named for the vessels it takes.

clue.text: Think again about swilling cider, son!

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: swilling suggests sloshing the drink around, so the letters of cider and son are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent tells a son to think twice about gulping cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the definition, but it gives the short word for concerning; 'swilling' signals the anagram of the drink and the son.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think about something again and perhaps change one's mind.

clue.text: Wander round as dog without tail?

indicators.note: without tail says the final letter of the dog's name is dropped

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A tailless dog roams about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' drops the last R of ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rove is to roam or wander about aimlessly.

clue.text: Argument against leads to stress, we hear

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: we hear says a word is to be taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: tension is a synonym of stress

explanation.surface: A quarrel ends up causing strain, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns TENSION into the same-sounding ending TENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a contention is a point argued or a dispute.

clue.text: Design event at Edinburgh?

definitions.meaning: a picture inked into the skin
the Edinburgh Military ..., an annual display of military bands at Edinburgh Castle

explanation.surface: A design for a happening in the Scottish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a skin decoration and a military display such as Edinburgh's famous one.

clue.text: Boring noise that comes with percussion instrument

parts.note: a hum is a low continuous noise
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A dull sound accompanied by drumming.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something humdrum is dull, monotonous and lacking excitement.

clue.text: See me mooching around in return journey?

indicators.note: around suggests moving about, so the letters of me mooching are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees a person loafing about on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the anagram; 'See' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A homecoming is a return to one's home, a journey back.

clue.text: There's a boom when it goes over one

definitions.text: There's a boom when it goes over one

parts.words: There's a boom when it goes over one
parts.note: an aircraft breaking the sound barrier, passing speed ratio one, produces a sonic boom

explanation.surface: Something explodes when it tips past a single unit, like a market boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom' suggests economic growth, but it is the sonic boom at the speed of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This ratio of speed to the speed of sound exceeds one at supersonic speed, causing a sonic boom.

clue.text: Join forces in summer get-together

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words summer get-together

explanation.surface: Groups combine at a gathering in the warm months.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to merge is to combine or unite into one.

clue.text: Mollycoddles maiden in rags?

indicators.note: in says the maiden's letter goes inside the word for rags

parts.note: rags is slang for newspapers, papers
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a young woman dressed in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside PAPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to pamper is to indulge or spoil someone with excessive care.

clue.text: Bits to fasten up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to strap is to fasten with a belt

explanation.surface: Pieces needed to fix something together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns STRAP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: parts are pieces or components of a whole.

clue.text: Some of these dances — one may get carried away!

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some dances are so thrilling that a dancer gets carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried away' looks like enthusiasm, but a sedan chair was carried by bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat borne on poles, so a passenger in one is literally carried.

clue.text: Club card provided by Head of Membership

indicators.note: Head of picks out the opening letter of the word Membership

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A club's membership secretary hands over a card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but it is a heavy weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a spiked or heavy-headed club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Crazy about one girl

indicators.note: about says the word for crazy goes around the numeral

parts.note: mad means crazy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about a particular girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MAD around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is an old-fashioned or poetic word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Entrance blocked at front by a stone

indicators.note: blocked at front by says the entrance word has a placed before it

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A gateway is barred by a stone in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious stone, a variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: A throne to be destroyed? Not this one!

indicators.note: to be destroyed says the letters of A throne are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary insists on smashing a throne, though not this particular one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be destroyed' signals the anagram of A THRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for a different one rather than this one is asking for an alternative item.

clue.text: I cheat terribly, last character in school to be moral

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of I cheat are rearranged
last character in picks the final letter of the word school

explanation.surface: A pupil confesses to cheating badly in a school with high principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges ICHEAT into ETHICA, and 'last character in' adds L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being ethical means acting according to sound moral principles.

clue.text: Pardon prisoner getting discharged

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a duty discharged is done, completed

explanation.surface: A convict is pardoned and released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' looks like release from jail, but it means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to condone is to overlook or forgive an offence.

clue.text: Son, one who blabs — a sneaky type

parts.note: someone who blabs is a talker

explanation.surface: A boy who tells tales is a bit of a sneak.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is someone who furtively follows another person, a sneaky type.

clue.text: Poor national charity gets to moan

parts.note: lame means poor or feeble, as in a lame excuse
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A weak charity ends up complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity preserving historic buildings and land.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to moan or wail in grief or complaint.

clue.text: Second sign delivered in extremes of merriment

indicators.note: delivered in says the sign is placed within the letters that follow
extremes of picks the first and last letters of merriment

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A portent arrives in the midst of festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' gives M and T, with OMEN placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a second is a very short time, an instant.

clue.text: Move slowly as monster that's lost leg

indicators.note: that's lost says the leg side letters are removed from the monster

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster
leg and on both name the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A one-legged creature shuffles along.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side; 'that's lost' removes ON from DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag is to proceed tediously slowly, as time drags.

clue.text: Regarding saint wearing a halo

indicators.note: wearing says the saint sits inside, wrapped by the other letters

parts.note: a halo is a ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A holy figure depicted with a glowing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts ST inside A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means concerning or with respect to a matter.

clue.text: He searched all over the place — reaction with nothing found?

indicators.note: all over the place suggests disorder, so the letters of He searched are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man hunts high and low and is disappointed when nothing turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' looks like the search itself, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British expression of mock sympathy for bad luck, apt when a search fails.

clue.text: Five not appearing in new season

indicators.note: not appearing in says the numeral is removed from the word for new

parts.note: novel means new
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: The quintet is absent from the fresh season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not appearing in' drops V from NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the festive season.

clue.text: Rule good for top people with external connection

indicators.note: with external says the connection word sits on the outside of the other letters

parts.note: a relation is a connection
U means upper-class, suitable for top people

explanation.surface: A rule benefiting the elite, with links to outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with external' wraps RELATION around G and U. U for upper-class is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a regulation is an official rule or directive.
